Suga and colleagues (261) demonstrated that only 31% of subjects displayed recruitment of fast-twitch fibers during occlusion training at 20% of 1RM compared with 70% of subjects who performed nonoccluded training at 65% of 1RM. Considering that BFR at this intensity (20% of 1RM) has been shown to increase muscle growth to an extent similar to, or greater than, high-intensity resistance training (150, 306), the anabolic effects seemingly cannot be solely a function of equal fiber recruitment.
